title: Tail latency atlas: p95/p99 breakdowns by route, model, and region
creator: Isha Menon
description: Produce a single-pane 'Tail latency atlas' that surfaces p95 and p99 latency metrics sliced by API route, model variant, and region. The atlas should combine live telemetry (rollups) with inferbench-derived baseline profiles and allow teams to quickly identify regressions, capacity hotspots, and the most cost-sensitive endpoints. This ticket covers backend metric derivation, storage/rollup strategy, a lightweight API for the Console, and a first-pass visualization in the Console's Observability section.
acceptance_criteria: Backend emits p50/p95/p99 rollups per (route, model, region) in 1m and 5m windows
Rollups stored in time-series store and queryable by Console API with <=2s query latency for 90% of requests
Console view shows heatmap + sparklines for selected route/model/region and supports baseline comparison vs inferbench profile
Automated alerting rule templates provided for p99 regressions (configurable thresholds and lookback)
Documentation: runbook, cost estimate, and migration notes for downstream dashboards
implementation_notes: Add new telemetry emitter node that aggregates per-request latency and emits quantile sketches (DDSketch) and histogram rollups to clickhouse/tsdb
Store both raw sketch blobs and pre-aggregated quantiles for 1m/5m/1h windows to balance resolution and query cost
Leverage existing slice keys: route, model, region, instance_type, priority_tier
Sampling strategy: 100% for synthetic/regression harness traffic; 5-10% stratified sampling for production traffic with higher sampling on high-traffic routes
Backfill: join inferbench baseline profiles during query time rather than writing large backfilled tables
Provide a thin aggregation API with query params: start, end, resolution, quantiles=[0.5,0.95,0.99], group_by=[route,model,region]
Precompute delta vs baseline on background job for frequently viewed slices; fallback to on-the-fly compare for ad-hoc slices
Ensure metrics are tagged with model variant and quantization flags to avoid conflating compatible model variants
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): Implement telemetry emitter and storage schema; wire inferbench baseline lookup
Phase 2 (week 3): Build Console API and lightweight heatmap UI behind feature flag; expose query sampling controls
Phase 3 (week 4): Enable alert templates and integrate with runbooks; start canary for internal teams
Phase 4 (week 5): Gradual enablement for all customers; monitor cost and adjust rollup cadence
Rollback: disable atlas UI and stop background delta job; metrics ingestion remains intact
comments: 2025-03-02 - Isha Menon: Kickoff with Observability and Runtime teams. Agreed to use DDSketch for production quantiles and full histograms for synthetic harness traffic.
2025-03-04 - Luca Alvarez: Proof-of-concept emitter implemented; local end-to-end shows p95/p99 alignment with inferbench for synthetic workloads. Next: storage schema review.
2025-03-06 - PM (Riley Chen): Requested that alerts be configurable per-customer AND per-route. Also asked for an exportable CSV for exec reports.
2025-03-09 - Design (Maya Ortiz): Shared wireframe for heatmap + detail panel. UX asks for quick toggles: compare-to-baseline, time-shift, and model-variant filter.
2025-03-11 - Security (A. Patel): Confirmed no PII in latency payloads. Recommended symmetric encryption in transit, and storing only aggregated sketches in ClickHouse.
2025-03-12 - Luca Alvarez: Started Console API endpoints; feature flag 'tail-latency-atlas' added to config service. Internal canary targeting infra and platform teams next week.
notes: Trade-offs: storing both sketches and precomputed quantiles increases storage but reduces query latency for the Console. We'll monitor costs closely and prune older raw sketches after 90 days.
Open question: whether to expose p99.9 for high-sensitivity routes; recommend adding as future enhancement if storage/query budget allows.
Related initiative: sync with Dedicated autoscaler team to correlate quantile spikes with utilization metrics.
